title: Episode 1: The Phone Call
text:
KATIE: Hello?
SAL: Hi, is that Katie?
KATIE: Oh, hi Sal! How are you?
SAL: Fine, Katie. I’m fine. What about you?
KATIE: Oh, I’m okay.
SAL: Katie, have you thought about my suggestion? About coming out to California?
KATIE: I don’t know, Sal. I’ve thought about it every day. But I have my job here, and Mark… I don’t know.
SAL: Katie, you’re my cousin. I’m going to be honest with you. You hate your life there in England. You hate your job. You spend your free time watching football with Mark, and with Mark’s friends. You’re depressed. You’re depressed Katie, and you need a change.
KATIE: I know, I know. You’re right...It’s just... It’s just... I don’t know.
SAL: Katie. Just come out here for a visit. This summer. You’ll see, you’ll love it! We’ll have fun! I haven’t seen you since last summer.
MARK: KATIEEE!
KATIE: Sal, I have to go. Mark’s here.
MARK: Who was that?
KATIE: Just my cousin Sal.
MARK: Well, come on.
KATIE: What?
MARK: The match starts in ten minutes. We’re going to Chris’ house. They’re waiting in the car!
KATIE: Mark, I...
MARK: What?
KATIE: Nothing. Let’s go.

title: Episode 2: The Football Match
text:
MARK: Hi! We’re here. We’re a bit late – Katie’s fault as always!
KATIE: Hi Chris! Hi everyone.
BOYS: Hello Katie. Hi Mark.
MARK: Have I missed anything?
CHRIS: No, it’s just starting now. Put your jackets in my bedroom.
MARK: Good. Phew. Katie, could you take my jacket?
KATIE: Yes, sure.
MARK: Isn’t there any food or drink?
CHRIS: What? Oh, yeah, there are some drinks in the fridge. And some crisps on the table… somewhere.
MARK: Would you mind getting them Katie?
KATIE: Yes, of course.
KATIE: Here are the drinks. And the crisps.
BOYS: Ah, thanks Katie. That’s great. Cheers.
CHRIS: Hey, guys. I’ve got some sausage rolls too. They’re in the fridge. Want some?
MARK: Oh yeah!
CHRIS: Katie, the sausage rolls are in the fridge, top shelf. Can you bring them?
KATIE: Oh, all right.
BOYS: GOAL!
KATIE: What was it? A goal?
MARK: Yes! Yes! Can’t believe you missed it.
CHRIS: It was a great goal, Katie.
KATIE: Oh. Well, I was getting the sausage rolls. Since I’m the only one on my feet...
MARK: Great, great. Sausage roll time. Do you mind if I have two, Chris?
CHRIS: No problem Mark.
MARK: Katie, could you pass me...?
KATIE: Why don’t you get them Mark? They’re right there on the table!
[silence]
MARK: Come on Katie, don’t be like that.
KATIE: Like what? Have you ever thought about what I’d like to do on a Saturday night?
MARK: I thought you liked football.
KATIE: That’s not the point! You… you… You know what? Forget it. I’m leaving.
[silence]
CHRIS: Whoa.
MARK: Don’t worry, she’ll be okay. She needs to calm down, that’s all. Pass me a sausage roll, Chris!

title: Episode 3: Another Day at Work
text:
CUSTOMER 1: Hello 752319.
KATIE: Good morning, my name’s Katie and I’m phoning from ‘Speedy Net’. Do you have an Internet connection at home?
CUSTOMER 1: Hello, um, yes I do have Internet, thanks.
KATIE: Would you be interested in changing to Speedy Net сonnection? We have some excellent offers this month.
CUSTOMER 1: No thanks, I’m happy with what I’ve got. Thanks, bye.
KATIE: Ok, fine.
CUSTOMER 2: Hello?
KATIE: Hello. My name’s Katie and I’m phoning from ‘Speedy Net’. Do you have an Internet connection at home?
CUSTOMER 2: Yes, I do thanks, and it’s really not a good time for me right now.
KATIE: Ok, yes, I can hear you’re busy. Can I call back later?
CUSTOMER 2: No, please don’t. I don’t want to change my Internet server thanks. Bye!
KATIE: Hello. My name’s Katie and I’m phoning from ‘Speedy Net’. Do you have an Internet connection at home?
CUSTOMER 3: Listen, I’m sick of you lot! I don’t want the Internet... I don’t want new windows... I don’t want cable TV... I don’t want any of it. Will you just stop phoning me?
KATIE: I’m sorry sir, but there’s no need to be so rude....
CUSTOMER 3: But it’s every day! You lot phone me up trying to sell me things I don’t even want... I’m sick of it!
KATIE: Well, you’re not the only one! Ahhhh!
MANAGER: Katie can I speak to you in my office please? I think you know why!
SAL: Hi, it’s Sal. I can’t take your call right now but leave a message and I’ll call right back.
KATIE: Sal? It’s Katie. You’re right. I’m fed up. I’m coming to California!

title: Episode 4: The Argument
text:
KATIE: Could you please turn the TV off? I have something to say.
MARK: Can it wait? It’s just that the football results are coming soon...
KATIE: No it can’t wait!
[Katie turns the TV off.]
MARK: Katie, I hate it when you do that.
KATIE: Well, this is very important and I can’t do it with the TV on!
MARK: So...?
KATIE: I’m going to America. To California, to visit my cousin Sal.
MARK: California? When? For how long?
KATIE: For a couple of months, maybe more.
MARK: What?! What about your job?
KATIE: I quit my job this morning.
MARK: Wait a minute. Are you saying you actually planned this?
KATIE: I wanted to tell you a couple of days ago but I couldn’t. I’m sorry, but I need a change. I’m not happy here.
MARK: What do you mean? What’s wrong with your life here? What about us?
KATIE: This isn’t easy for me to say Mark but I think we’re part of the problem. There is no “us”. It’s always you. Your interests. Your life. Your friends.
MARK: That’s not true!
KATIE: Yes, it is true Mark. You’re too selfish to realise it.
MARK: Katie, I’ve worked all day today. I’m too tired for this.
KATIE: I worked all day too, you know. You see? You’re being selfish again.
MARK: You know what? Forget it. Go home to your mum and we can talk tomorrow.
KATIE: My plane leaves tomorrow.
MARK: I can’t believe this.
KATIE: Mark, I...
MARK: Ok. Fine. Fine. Get out. Goodbye.
KATIE: Goodbye Mark.
MARK: You’re making a big mistake Katie! A VERY BIG mistake!

title: Episode 5: At the Airport
text:
(CHECK-IN ATTENDANT, hereafter CHECK-IN ATT.)
CHECK-IN ATT.: Hello, where are you travelling to?
KATIE: Los Angeles.
CHECK-IN ATT.: Can I see your passport please? Ok that’s fine. How many bags are you checking in?
KATIE: Just these two.
CHECK-IN ATT.: Did you pack the bags yourself?
KATIE: Yes. Yes, I did.
CHECK-IN ATT.: Have you got anything sharp in your hand luggage? Scissors? A knife?
KATIE: No, no, I haven’t.
CHECK-IN ATT.: Would you prefer a window or an aisle seat?
KATIE: Window please.
MARK: Katie! Katie! There you are! Phew!
KATIE: Oh! What are you doing here Mark?
MARK: Katie. You’re still here. Good.
CHECK-IN ATT.: Excuse me, sorry to interrupt. Here’s your boarding pass. Your flight boards at 8.20 from gate number 37. Have a nice flight!
KATIE: Thanks.
KATIE: Mark, please...
MARK: I’ve just come... to say sorry...
KATIE: Mark...
MARK: ...for shouting at you before.
KATIE: That’s okay.
MARK: Will you call me from California?
KATIE: Of course I will.
ANNOUNCER: Will all passengers on flight BA432 to Los Angeles please go to gate 37 where your plane is ready for boarding.
KATIE: That’s my plane. I have to go.
MARK: OK. Bye.
KATIE: Bye. MARK: No, wait. Katie!
KATIE: Yes?
MARK: I’ve acted like an idiot. I love you.
KATIE: Oh... Mark. Don’t...
MARK: Just, just don’t... don’t forget me. Don’t be late for your plane. Call me from California.
KATIE: Thanks Mark. I will. Bye.
MARK: Bye.

title: Episode 6: On the Plane
text:
(MM = Michael Mensah)
KATIE: This is silly.
MM: Excuse me.
KATIE: Yes?
MM: I’m in the seat next to you. Can I just...?
KATIE: Of course. Sorry.
MM: Is it your first visit to Los Angeles?
KATIE: What? Me? Oh. Yes. Yes it is.
MM: You’ll like it.
KATIE: Yeah. Well. Thanks.
MM: Ah, airplane food. It’s better now than in the past.
KATIE: Would you like my dessert? I’m not very hungry.
MM: Thanks!
KATIE: Are you from the US?
MM: No, I’m originally from Ghana. But I’ve lived in LA for a long time.
KATIE: Oh. Why were you in England?
MM: For a poetry festival.
KATIE: Poetry? That’s interesting. Do you write poetry?
MM: A little. Why are you going to the States?
KATIE: To change my life.
MM: Sounds exciting.
KATIE: I don’t know. I’m a bit nervous.
MM: ‘I took the road less traveled by, And that has made all the difference.’
KATIE: What?
MM: It’s from a poem, by Robert Frost. It’s about making decisions. And travelling.
KATIE: Oh. Thanks.
MM: My name’s Michael Mensah by the way.
KATIE: I’m Katie.
MM: Nice to meet you Katie.
KATIE: Yes. Yes, nice to meet you.
MM: Hey, look. I’ve got a book of Robert Frost’s poetry here, if you want to read the whole poem.
KATIE: Thanks.
MM: No problem, it helps pass the time.

title: Episode 7: Arrival!
text:
(LA = Loudspeaker announcer)
(CO = Customs Officer)
LA: Would all passengers please have your passports ready as you pass through United States customs.
CO: Excuse me, miss?
KATIE: Sorry, yes. Me?
CO: We’ll need to check your bags miss.
KATIE: Oh. OK.
CO: Your passport too please miss.
KATIE: Here you are.
CO: Where did you fly from today?
KATIE: Excuse me, I...?
CO: Where did you fly from today?
KATIE: London. England.
CO: What’s this?
KATIE: Just a bottle of water.
CO: Can you drink some of it please for me?
KATIE: Sure. See?
CO: Thank you. What’s this?
KATIE: What’s what?
CO: This.
KATIE: It’s... it’s an apple.
CO: No apples allowed miss. I’m going to have to dispose of this item.
KATIE: But it’s only an apple!
CO: Sorry miss, but those are the rules. No apples or similar fruit allowed. What’s this?
KATIE: It’s a present. For my cousin.
CO: Open it please.
KATIE: I can’t believe this. Is this really necessary?
CO: Yes. Hmm. OK.
KATIE: Satisfied?
CO: Yes. That will be all. You can go. Have a nice day.
KATIE: Sorry?
CO: I said, have a nice day. Good bye.
KATIE: Thank you. Bye.
SAL: Katieee!

title: Episode 8: Sal and Rich
text:
KATIE: Sal, who’s that guy standing by the car?
SAL: That’s Rich!
RICH: Heey babe! You saw me!
SAL: I did darling! [Sal gives Rich a kiss] Rich, this is my cousin Katie. Katie, this is my boyfriend, Rich.
RICH: Hi Katie, good to meet you. I have heard lots of things about you.
KATIE: Hello Rich. I hope you haven’t been waiting too long.
RICH: Don’t worry, Sal’s not a good example of British punctuality. I’m used to waiting.
SAL: Are you? Hmm. I’ll go and pay for the parking ticket at the machine over there.
RICH: Okay baabe! You do know where it is, right?
SAL: Very funny! [Sal walks over to the machine]
RICH: Sooooo, Katie.
KATIE: Hi again.
RICH: You’re even prettier in real life than in the photos Sal showed me.
KATIE: [Laughs w​​​​ith embarrassment] Sal told me you work in a bar.
RICH: Oh, did she? What she meant to say was that I own a club.
KATIE: Oh, sorry. Anyway, thanks a lot for coming to the airport to get me.
RICH: No problem honey. Any time. Anything for a beautiful lady.
KATIE: Here’s Sal.
SAL: Right, all paid. Let’s go. What was that about a beautiful lady? Are you talking about me again Rich? [Sal laughs]
RICH: That’s right darling. Okay. Let’s go!
SAL: So, tell me all about England…

title: Episode 9: The New Job
text:
SAL: Hi! I’m home.
KATIE: Oh, hi Sal. How did the acting audition go?
SAL: Not very well. I don’t think I got the part.
KATIE: Oh well, I’m sure something will come up.
SAL: What’s wrong with you? You’re not looking very happy.
KATIE: What... oh no, no, nothing.
SAL: Come on, Katie. What is it?
KATIE: It’s just that... I’ve been here a month now, and it’s been great. I mean, really great. Everyone is so nice, LA is great. Your friends are great.
SAL: So?
KATIE: I... I haven’t got any more money!
SAL: Hey... don’t worry.
KATIE: Oh, Sal... but I do worry. You can’t put me up at your place forever. And I don’t... I really don’t want to go back to England.
SAL: Listen... oh wait, hold on a second.
RICH: Hey baaabe. Hi Katie.
SAL: Hi Rich.
RICH: Whassup with you two lovely ladies? You’re looking pretty depressed.
SAL: Katie’s running out of money. She doesn’t want to go back to England and that horrible ex-boyfriend.
KATIE: Sal!
SAL: So? It’s true.
RICH: Yeah. Yeah! We need a new waitress at the club actually – and I think I know just the person...
SAL: You see! I knew Rich could help out.
KATIE: I... er... I don’t know.
RICH: Hey, you’d be great. Bring some British class into the place. Since Beckham came to LA everyone is just crazy about the English. And don’t worry, I can teach you… everything.
SAL: Isn’t that great? Then you can stay with me!
RICH: So, Katie. Whaddaya say? Wanna come and work at my club?
KATIE: Well... okay then.
SAL: Rich, this is great. You’re a darling.
RICH: Yeah. It’s going to work out... perfectly.

title: Episode 10: The Favour
text:
KATIE: Hi Sal! I’m exhausted, what a night!
SAL: Was the club busy?
KATIE: Busy? It was absolutely packed, especially after the football game.
SAL: Anyone famous there? David Beckham perhaps?
KATIE: No. I don’t think he and Victoria go to places like The Red Palace.
SAL: I don’t know... it’s quite a classy club.
KATIE: Hey Sal, you sound terrible. What’s up?
SAL: I don’t know. I think it’s just a cold, but I’ve got a sore throat, a cough, a runny nose... everything!
KATIE: Oh, poor you, I’ll make you a honey and lemon drink, that should help.
KATIE: Oh, Sal, haven’t you got that big audition tomorrow, for the ice-cream ad?
SAL: Yeah, I have – but I can’t go like this...
SAL: Hey, Katie.... I don’t suppose...?
KATIE: Oh no, no, no, no. I know what you’re thinking.
SAL: But they really need an English girl for this one...
KATIE: You know I can’t act.
SAL: ...and I promised my agent I’d go – he’s completely counting on me. At least, if you go, I won’t let him down completely.
KATIE: Hmm. Here’s your honey and lemon drink.
SAL: Look, you don’t have to get the part. That doesn’t matter... Thanks for the drink. Ahh. Fantastic. You’re an angel... Listen, you just go and that way I don’t look bad. And my agent doesn’t look bad.
KATIE: Well, actually I didn’t have any plans for tomorrow morning so I guess I could go.
SAL: Wow! You really are an angel!
KATIE: Don’t be silly Sal! You’ll have to tell me what to do.
SAL: No problem. You just have to walk around with an ice cream in your hand, and say something in a British accent.
KATIE: Huh, well it doesn’t sound too difficult! I’ll do my best.
SAL: Thanks Katie. I owe you one.

title: Episode 11: The Audition
text:
(DIR = Director)
(MM = Michael Mensah)
DIR: Ok, ok! That’s it everyone. Time for a break! Auditions continue in fifteen
minutes!
KATIE: What do I do now?
DIR: What do you do now? You wait. I dunno, get a bagel or something. We’ll let you know.
KATIE: Ok, so I’ll just go over there...
DIR: Whatever. You do whatever you like, just stay outta my way.
KATIE: Ok.
MM: Katie?
KATIE: Hello? Oh wow!
MM: We met on the plane over here. I’m Mike, Michael Mensah – do you remember me? We sat next to each other on the plane.
KATIE: Of course.
MM: I was thinking about you the other day. What a coincidence! How are things? You look... great.
KATIE: Thanks, I...
MM: I mean, you look happier than... on the plane before.
KATIE: Oh, I see.
MM: You’re here for the acting job?
KATIE: Well, yeah. I won’t get it though.
MM: I think you’re perfect for it.
KATIE: Really? The director is a bit – I don’t think he likes me.
MM: Who, Chuck? Don’t worry about him. He’s really nice actually.
KATIE: What are you doing here? Are you an actor and a poet?
MM: Oh, no no. I’m the writer.
KATIE: You write commercials?
MM: Yes, well, I have to make money somehow.
MM: So, are you taking the road less travelled?
KATIE: The... what? The road less travelled?
MM: You know, from the poem you read on the plane.
KATIE: Oh! Yeah, I guess I am.
MM: So, how are things going? Do you regret your decision to come here?
KATIE: No. No. Not at all. Everything’s great. I’m working at a club. I’m making friends.
MM: Oh good. I’m glad.
KATIE: Well, I’d better...

title: Episode 12: Surprises
text:
KATIE: Hi, I’m home!
SAL: Hi Katie. How did it go?
KATIE: It was really fun! You’re not going to believe this, but...
SAL: You actually got the job?!
KATIE: Yeah. I can’t believe it either!
SAL: Wow... that’s great. I mean it... that’s amazing Katie. Well done you!
KATIE: Oh, thanks Sal. I feel a bit bad, I mean...
SAL: Don’t be silly Katie.
KATIE: Are you sure you don’t mind?
SAL: Of course not. It was me who asked you to go to the audition in the first place. I’ll make you a cuppa and you can tell me all about it.
KATIE: Sal, do you remember the poet guy I told you about? The guy I met on the plane over here?
SAL: Yeah, course I do; ‘The Road Less Travelled’ man. How could I possibly forget? You spoke about him non-stop for the first week!
KATIE: I didn’t, but anyway, he was there!
SAL: Where?
KATIE: At the audition! He wrote the commercial.
SAL: No way! What a coincidence. So, was it good to see him again?
KATIE: Yeah, it was. Actually it was really nice...
SAL: So, are you going to see him again?
KATIE: Well…
SAL: Ooooooooh.
SAL: Hello? Oh, Hi Mark! Hold on a second...
SAL: It’s Mark, again.
KATIE: Tell him I’m not here.
SAL: Ok... Sorry, hi Mark. Umm... Actually she’s not here at the moment. Yes, I know. I’ll give her the message... Wait a second... What? What, here? You’re in LA? Yes, I can tell her to call you at your hotel. OK...
KATIE: What did he say?
SAL: He’s here. In the United States. He said he’s come to see you.
KATIE: Oh no.

title: Episode 13: The Fight
text:
RICH: What a night, huh?
KATIE: Yeah, it’s busy all right.
RICH: You’ve got a new customer on table 14.
KATIE: Ok, Rich – thanks.
KATIE: [sharp intake of breath]
MARK: Hi Katie.
KATIE: Mark... I... you’re here. What a surprise. How did you find me?
MARK: It wasn’t hard, you know. I’m not as stupid as you think.
KATIE: Mark. I’m working right now. I... I can’t talk.
MARK: You call this a job? Look at this place. What a mess.
KATIE: What do you want Mark?
MARK: To talk.
KATIE: We’re talking.
MARK: Katie, I flew all the way here to see you.
KATIE: I can see that.
MARK: To come and take you back home. Back to England. Back to Slough.
KATIE: I can’t Mark. I can’t go back.
MARK: Why not?
KATIE: I told you before, it’s over. I’m sorry, I can’t speak to you now... I...
MARK: No, we’re gonna talk about this NOW! Your place is back home, with your family, with your job, in your country. Now get your things, we’re leaving.
RICH: Is there a problem here?
MARK: Oh perfect. Who’s this? Your new American boyfriend?
KATIE: Mark, stop being...
MARK: Leave us alone. We’re leaving.
RICH: She’s not going anywhere unless she wants to.
MARK: Oh, yeah?
KATIE: Mark, no... I can’t...
RICH: I said, leave her alone.
MARK: What an idiot.
KATIE: Mark...
MARK: Shut UP, Katie and GET-YOUR-THINGS.
RICH: OK, that’s enough. Get out.
MARK: Who are you? The bodyguard?
RICH: Nope. I’m the owner of this place.
MARK: Hey... get off me! GET OFF! LET ME GO!
RICH: Don’t worry everyone – this gentleman was just leaving. Right?
MARK: Uhnnngg.

title: Episode 14: The Parking Lot
text:
RICH: Hey, hey, don’t worry. He’s gone and I don’t think he’ll be coming back to The Red Palace in a hurry.
KATIE: Thanks Rich. I’m so sorry.
RICH: Hey, babe... it’s not your fault. You didn’t know your crazy ex was going to show up here.
KATIE: I know... but he really wasn’t crazy before. In fact he was really sensible.
RICH: Well, looks like he was crazy. Crazy for you anyway.
KATIE: Mmm.
RICH: I’m not surprised.
KATIE: What?
RICH: Nothing babe. Are you okay?
KATIE: Yeah, but, you know, maybe I should have just stayed in England...
RICH: You did the right thing.
KATIE: I don’t know what I’m doing here any more.
RICH: Come on, stop that, come here, you need a hug. Better?
KATIE: Much better, thanks... Oh, I’m so sorry, you must think I’m a total...
RICH: Shhh, I think you’re a great girl, just a bit lost... and I think you’ve taken a brave step, and I think that sooner or later you’ll find your feet here.
KATIE: Really...? You think that?
RICH: I do babe. I really do.
KATIE: I’m so confused...
RICH: Shhhh... come here…
KATIE: We can’t do this, Rich.
RICH: You’re upset. I shouldn’t have kissed you.
KATIE: No, it’s okay.
RICH: You just looked so beautiful. I’ve wanted to kiss you since...
KATIE: Stop. Just stop... it was nice... but you’re... we can’t just...
RICH: I know. Come on, the others will be wondering where we are.

title: Episode 15: Confessions
text:
SAL: Katie, do you have a minute?
KATIE: What...? Oh, yeah. Hi Sal.
SAL: Is everything all right?
KATIE: Fine... everything’s fine.
SAL: I mean... Rich told me you took a couple of days off and you’re not talking to anyone.
KATIE: Nothing. I’m just worried about Mark I guess.
SAL: Oh, I know. What a nightmare. Have you heard from him since Rich threw him out of the club?
KATIE: No. I hope he’s gone back to England but I really don’t want to think about it anymore.
SAL: Well, there’s something I’ve been meaning to tell you.
KATIE: Me too. I have to tell you something too.
SAL: Okay. You go first.
KATIE: No, you started.
SAL: Okay, you know Rich and I have been together for almost two years now.
KATIE: Yes…
SAL: And he’s great, isn’t he great?
KATIE: Yes...
SAL: And you know I want to stay here, but I don’t have papers, right?
KATIE: Errr… yes.
SAL: Well... last night I asked Rich to marry me!
KATIE: You WHAT????
SAL: I asked him to marry me. I know it’s not traditional, but who cares? And do you know what he said?
KATIE: Errr... what did he say?
SAL: He said YES! And I wanted YOU to be the first person to know. So, what do you think? Me and Rich, husband and wife! Can you BELIEVE it?
KATIE: Wow. No, I mean... yes. That’s great news. I’m glad for you.
SAL: You look a little pale.
KATIE: NO... no. That’s great.
SAL: OK. Phew. That felt good. To tell someone. Now your turn. What did you want to tell me?
KATIE: Nothing. I can’t remember now.
SAL: Well, I’m sure it will come back. Anyway, I’m soooo happy. I think it’s the best decision I ever made. Don’t you Katie? I mean, you made the decision to come here, I made the decision to get married. It’s going to be great!
KATIE: Yeah…
